 Order No.03 Dated- 16.06.2023
 Heard the parties.

The petitioner has moved this Court for grant of bail in connection with Complaint Case No. 720 of 2021 registered under sections 323/498A of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3/4 of D.P.
Act.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that consequent upon the petitioner submitting that he is willing to reside with the opposite party no.2 though she has demonstrated reluctance and the submission made by the opposite party no.2 that the opposite party no.2 is willing to live with the petitioner, a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 26.04.2023 released the petitioner on provisional bail till 16.06.2023 on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- with two sureties.
In the meantime, mediation took place and the same failed.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner being the husband of the opposite party no.2-informant after the marriage demanded Rs.50,000/- and if the alleged demand is not fulfilled, the petitioner will commit the murder of his wife-informant and throw her dead body and solemnize second marriage.

There is specific allegation against the petitioner that after assaulting his wife, the petitioner along with co- accused persons snatched her earring and other ornaments and ousted her from his house.
It is further submitted that the allegations against the petitioner are all false and the petitioner is ready Nitya Nand Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr. ... ...

It is next submitted that the petitioner was in custody since 07.02.2023 to 26.04.2023 and the petitioner is a daily wage worker.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner be admitted to bail.

The learned Addl. P.P. and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer for bail and submits that the petitioner has played fraud upon the Court as he undertook before the Court in Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1157 of 2022 to pay Rs.1,00,000/- as ad interim victim compensation and upon his undertaking, the prayer of anticipatory bail was allowed but after getting the breather in shape of said order passed in Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1157 of 2022, the petitioner did not deposit Rs.1,00,000/- nor appeared before the learned trial court within the stipulated time but subsequently, he surrendered and though made a false submission in this bail petition that he is ready and willing to keep his wife with full dignity and honour but did not cooperate with the mediation resulting in mediation having been failed which is evident from the report submitted by the Mediator appointed by District Legal Services Authority, Civil Court, Godda.
It is next submitted that keeping in view the serious nature of allegation and his dishonest character, there is every chance of the petitioner tampering with evidence and creating nuisance.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner ought not to be admitted to bail.

Considering the serious nature of allegation against the petitioner and the conduct of the petitioner,
this Court is not inclined to admit the petitioner on bail at this stage.
Accordingly, the prayer for bail of the above named petitioner is rejected.

The applicant is directed to surrender before the learned trial court today itself, failing which, the learned trial court is directed to take all coercive steps for apprehension of the petitioner for facing the trial.

In case, the petitioner surrenders before the learned trial court, the learned trial court is directed to take up the trial expeditiously and conclude the same preferably within a period of six months from the date of surrender/production of the petitioner on arrest before the learned trial court.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sonu-Gunjan/
